8.1: The Hebrew says “his house”; BSB specifies “his own palace.”
8.2: The Hebrew says “built” and repeats Solomon’s name; BSB says “rebuilt” and uses “him.”
8.3: The Hebrew says Solomon became strong against Hamath-zobah; BSB expresses this as capturing it.
8.8: The Hebrew says the Israelites did not destroy them; BSB says they were unable to destroy them.
8.10: The Hebrew explicitly says these officials ruled over the people; BSB calls them supervisors without expressing that object.
8.13: The Hebrew gives the daily requirement for offering according to Moses’ command; BSB supplies the clause “He observed.”
8.15: The Hebrew coordinates “every matter” and “the treasuries”; BSB makes the treasuries the subject of the matters concerned.
8.18: The Hebrew says Hiram sent ships and servants who knew the sea through his servants; BSB specifies captains and experienced crews.

9.1: The Hebrew says “riddles” and “in her heart”; BSB says “difficult questions” and “on her mind.”
9.2: The Hebrew says nothing was hidden from Solomon; BSB says nothing was too difficult for him.
9.4: The Hebrew describes his ascent by which he went up to the LORD’s house; BSB describes burnt offerings he presented there. The Hebrew separately mentions the clothing of the attendants and of the cupbearers.
9.11: The Hebrew says “the king’s house”; BSB specifies “the royal palace.”
9.12: The Hebrew says “besides what she had brought”; BSB says “far more than she had brought.”
9.13: The Hebrew says “in one year”; BSB says “each year.”
9.15: The Hebrew gives six hundred of gold without an explicit weight unit; BSB supplies “shekels.”
9.16: The Hebrew gives three hundred of gold without an explicit weight unit; BSB supplies “shekels.”
9.20: The Hebrew says silver was considered nothing in Solomon’s days; BSB also explicitly says there was no silver.
9.21: The Hebrew initially describes ships going to Tarshish; BSB initially calls them ships of Tarshish.
9.25: The Hebrew says twelve thousand horsemen; BSB says twelve thousand horses.
9.26: The Hebrew says “the River”; BSB identifies it as the Euphrates.
9.28: The Hebrew uses an active plural, “they brought horses for Solomon”; BSB uses the passive “Solomon’s horses were imported.”
9.31: The Hebrew says “they buried him”; BSB uses “was buried.”

10.1: The Hebrew repeats Shechem; BSB uses “there” for the second occurrence.
10.2: The Hebrew repeats Egypt and Jeroboam where BSB uses pronouns.
10.5: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed here; BSB explicitly names Rehoboam.
10.7: The Hebrew coordinates pleasing them and speaking good words to them; BSB makes speaking kindly the means of pleasing them.
10.8: The Hebrew describes the young men as standing before him; BSB describes them as serving him.
10.10: The Hebrew says “my little one” and “my father’s loins”; BSB specifies “my little finger” and says “waist.”
10.12: The Hebrew says they came on the third day; BSB initially says “after three days.”
10.14: The Hebrew begins the speech with “I will make your yoke heavy”; BSB begins with “My father made your yoke heavy.”
10.16: The Hebrew does not explicitly say that Israel “saw” this, as BSB does. It states that there is no inheritance in Jesse’s son and says “to your tents,” where BSB asks a question and says “go home.”
10.18: The Hebrew describes Rehoboam hastening to mount his chariot in order to flee; BSB explicitly says he escaped.

11.12: The Hebrew repeats “in every city and city”; BSB says “in all the cities.”
11.13: The Hebrew says they stood with “him”; BSB explicitly names Rehoboam.
11.15: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here and says “calves”; BSB names Jeroboam and specifies “calf idols.”
11.16: The Hebrew calls the LORD “the God of Israel”; BSB says “their God.”
11.23: The Hebrew says he sought many wives without explicitly saying “for them,” which BSB supplies.

12.8: The Hebrew says they will know “my service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands”; BSB explicitly frames this as learning the difference and refers to kings.
12.9: The Hebrew says “the king’s house”; BSB specifies “the royal palace.”
12.10: The Hebrew calls these men “runners” and says “the king’s house”; BSB says “guard” and “royal palace.”
12.11: The Hebrew says the runners came and carried them; BSB explicitly adds “with him” and identifies the objects as shields.
12.12: The Hebrew leaves him unnamed here and says there were good things in Judah; BSB names Rehoboam and describes conditions as good.
12.13: The Hebrew explicitly says he strengthened himself and reigned in Jerusalem; BSB combines this as establishing himself there.
12.14: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here; BSB names Rehoboam.

19.5: The Hebrew repeats “city by city”; BSB expresses this with “each.”
19.7: The Hebrew uses the image “lifting of faces” for partiality and explicitly mentions taking a bribe; BSB says “partiality” and “bribery.”
19.8: The Hebrew says they returned to Jerusalem; BSB says they lived there.
19.9: The Hebrew says “thus you shall do” and “with a whole heart”; BSB says “serve” and “wholeheartedly.”
19.10: The Hebrew says “between blood and blood” and distinguishes law, commandment, statutes, and judgments; BSB recasts these as bloodshed or other violations.

20.1: The Hebrew names Ammonites again in the final group; BSB names Meunites there.
20.2: The Hebrew says Aram; BSB says Edom.
20.4: The Hebrew repeats “the LORD” where BSB uses “Him.”
20.7: The Hebrew calls Abraham the one who loves You; BSB calls him Your friend.
20.9: The Hebrew repeats “this house”; BSB repeats “this temple.”
20.14: The Hebrew says the Spirit of the LORD was upon him in the assembly; BSB describes it coming upon him as he stood there.
20.16: The Hebrew says “behold, they are coming up”; BSB says “You will see them coming up.”
20.18: The Hebrew repeats “the LORD” where BSB uses “Him.”
20.21: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here; BSB names Jehoshaphat.
20.25: The Hebrew lists possessions, bodies, and precious objects; BSB describes goods and valuables found on the bodies.
20.26: The Hebrew says “they called” the place by that name; BSB uses the passive “is called.”
20.32: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here; BSB names Jehoshaphat.
20.36: The Hebrew says they made the ships in Ezion-geber; BSB uses the passive “these were built.”

21.1: The Hebrew repeats “his fathers”; BSB uses “them” for the second occurrence.
21.4: The Hebrew coordinates strengthening himself and killing his brothers; BSB makes killing them the means of strengthening himself.
21.6: The Hebrew says Ahab’s daughter was his wife; BSB describes his marrying her.
21.7: The Hebrew says “give him a lamp and his sons”; BSB says “maintain a lamp for David and his descendants.”
21.8: The Hebrew says “in his days”; BSB names Jehoram.
21.9: The Hebrew makes both Edom surrounding him and the chariot commanders objects of his attack; BSB makes his commanders people surrounded with him.
21.10: The Hebrew says Libnah rebelled from under his hand and leaves the following subject unnamed; BSB says “against his rule” and names Jehoram.
21.12: The Hebrew says the letter came “to him”; BSB names Jehoram.
21.15: The Hebrew speaks of many or severe illnesses and repeats the bowels; BSB consolidates this into a severe illness of the bowels.
21.17: The Hebrew says “the king’s house”; BSB specifies “the king’s palace.”
21.18: The Hebrew says the LORD struck “him”; BSB names Jehoram.
21.20: The Hebrew leaves him unnamed and says “they buried him”; BSB names Jehoram and uses “was buried.”

22.2: The Hebrew says forty-two years old and calls Athaliah Omri’s daughter; BSB says twenty-two and calls her Omri’s granddaughter.
22.3: The Hebrew says “he”; BSB names Ahaziah.
22.6: The Hebrew names the visiting king Azariah and calls Joram sick; BSB names the visitor Ahaziah and describes Joram as wounded.
22.9: The Hebrew leaves the searcher unnamed and uses unnamed plural subjects for capturing, bringing, and killing him; BSB names Jehu, specifies his soldiers, and uses passives. The Hebrew calls him Jehoshaphat’s son; BSB says grandson.
22.10: The Hebrew says “all the seed of the kingdom”; BSB says “all the royal heirs.”
22.11: The Hebrew says she did not kill him; BSB says she could not kill him.
22.12: The Hebrew leaves the hidden person unnamed here; BSB names Joash.

23.3: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed here; BSB names Jehoiada.
23.5: The Hebrew says “the king’s house” and “all the people”; BSB says “the royal palace” and “all the others.”
23.7: The Hebrew specifies being with the king when he comes in and goes out; BSB says “wherever he goes.”
23.10: The Hebrew says “the right shoulder” and “the left shoulder” of the house; BSB identifies these as its south and north sides.
23.11: The Hebrew leaves the initial plural subjects unnamed and names Jehoiada and his sons at the anointing; BSB names them at the beginning.
23.14: The Hebrew’s final prohibition is active, “do not kill her”; BSB uses “She must not be put to death.”
23.15: The Hebrew says “the king’s house”; BSB says “the palace grounds.”
23.16: The Hebrew orders the covenant parties as himself, all the people, and the king; BSB puts the king before the people.
23.19: The Hebrew describes someone unclean in any respect; BSB says “nothing unclean” entering “for any reason.”
23.20: The Hebrew says “the king” and “the king’s house”; BSB names Joash and says “the royal palace.”
23.21: The Hebrew says “they put Athaliah to death with the sword”; BSB uses the passive.

24.3: The Hebrew says Jehoiada took two wives “for him”; BSB interprets this as “for himself.”
24.8: The Hebrew uses active unnamed plural subjects for making and placing the chest; BSB uses passives.
24.9: The Hebrew uses an active plural for issuing the proclamation; BSB uses the passive.
24.13: The Hebrew uses an image of healing arising for the work through their hands; BSB says the repair work progressed.
24.14: The Hebrew uses an active plural for regularly offering burnt offerings; BSB uses the passive.
24.16: The Hebrew says “they buried him” and “His house”; BSB names Jehoiada, uses the passive, and says “His temple.”
24.19: The Hebrew leaves the sender unnamed but explicitly says “to the LORD”; BSB names the LORD as sender and then uses “Him.”
24.20: The Hebrew says God’s Spirit clothed Zechariah; BSB says it came upon him.
24.21: The Hebrew says “him”; BSB names Zechariah.
24.22: The Hebrew leaves the objects of the LORD’s seeing and requiring unexpressed; BSB explicitly adds “this” and “you.”
24.23: The Hebrew says “at the turn of the year” and “the king of Damascus”; BSB says “In the spring” and “their king in Damascus.”
24.24: The Hebrew says “they executed judgments on Joash”; BSB uses the passive.
24.25: The Hebrew says “sons of Jehoiada,” in the plural; BSB says “the son of Jehoiada.” The Hebrew uses active plural subjects for burying him, where BSB uses the passive.
24.26: The Hebrew says “him”; BSB names Joash.

30.4: The Hebrew says the matter was right in the eyes of the king and the assembly; BSB expresses this as pleasing them.
30.6: The Hebrew explicitly says the proclamation followed the king’s command; BSB introduces the words simply as what the letters read.
30.8: The Hebrew says “give a hand to the LORD”; BSB renders the image as “Submit to the LORD.”
30.12: The Hebrew says “the hand of God”; BSB says “the power of God.”
30.13: The Hebrew describes many people gathering and then calls them a very numerous assembly; BSB combines these descriptions.
30.15: The Hebrew says “the Passover” without explicitly specifying a lamb, which BSB supplies.
30.19: The Hebrew speaks of the purity of the holy place; BSB explicitly supplies “purification rules of the sanctuary.”
30.22: The Hebrew says Hezekiah spoke to the heart of the Levites and that they ate the festival; BSB says he encouraged them and they ate their assigned portion.
30.27: The Hebrew says their voice was heard, without naming the hearer; BSB explicitly names God.

31.2: The Hebrew says “appointed” and refers to the gates of the LORD’s camps; BSB says “reestablished” and “the LORD’s dwelling.”
31.6: The Hebrew repeats “heaps, heaps”; BSB says “large heaps.”
31.10: The Hebrew describes eating, being satisfied, and leaving much over; BSB expresses this as having enough to eat and plenty left over.
31.14: The Hebrew says “the holy things of holy things”; BSB says “the consecrated gifts.”
31.15: The Hebrew says “their brothers” and “great and small”; BSB specifies “their fellow priests” and “old and young.”
31.19: The Hebrew says “in every city and city”; BSB additionally distinguishes “any other city.”
31.21: The Hebrew explicitly says he acted with all his heart; BSB expresses this as being diligent.

32.1: The Hebrew coordinates “these acts and faithfulness”; BSB says “these acts of faithfulness.”
32.2: The Hebrew says his face was toward war against Jerusalem; BSB says he had come to make war against it.
32.5: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here and calls the structure the Millo; BSB names Hezekiah and says “supporting terraces.”
32.6: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here and says he spoke to their heart; BSB names Hezekiah and says he encouraged them.
32.8: The Hebrew says the people leaned on his words; BSB says they were strengthened by them.
32.16: The Hebrew says “his servants”; BSB specifies “the servants of Sennacherib.”
32.18: The Hebrew leaves the plural speakers unnamed and calls the language Judean; BSB names the Assyrians and calls the language Hebrew.
32.21: The Hebrew says “house of his god” and describes his killers as those who came from his inward parts; BSB says “temple of his god” and “his own sons.”
32.22: The Hebrew says He led them on every side; BSB says He gave them rest on every side.
32.25: The Hebrew says his heart was lifted up; BSB expresses this as pride.
32.31: The Hebrew ends with “his heart”; BSB explicitly names Hezekiah.
32.33: The Hebrew says “they buried him”; BSB uses “was buried.”

33.4: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here; BSB names Manasseh.
33.6: The Hebrew says he made his sons pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom; BSB says he sacrificed them and shortens the valley’s name.
33.7: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here and says “this house”; BSB names Manasseh and says “this temple.”
33.8: The Hebrew says “the foot of Israel”; BSB says “the feet of the Israelites.”
33.11: The Hebrew speaks of hooks in the plural without specifying the nose; BSB specifies a hook in his nose.
33.12: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed here and says he entreated the LORD’s face; BSB names Manasseh and says he sought the LORD’s favor.
33.13: The Hebrew leaves the hearer unnamed here; BSB explicitly names the LORD.
33.14: The Hebrew says “built” and leaves the subject unnamed; BSB says “rebuilt” and names Manasseh.
33.20: The Hebrew says “they buried him” and “his house”; BSB uses “was buried” and says “his palace.”
33.24: The Hebrew says “his servants” and “his house”; BSB names Amon and says “his palace.”
33.25: The Hebrew repeats “the people of the land”; BSB uses “they” for the second occurrence.

34.4: The Hebrew uses an active plural, “they tore down”; BSB uses the passive.

34.15: The Hebrew repeats the name Hilkiah and “the book”; BSB uses “he” and “it.”

34.30: The Hebrew orders the description “from great to small”; BSB says “small and great.”
34.31: The Hebrew says the king stood at his standing place; BSB specifies a pillar.
34.33: The Hebrew says “all his days”; BSB says “Throughout his reign.”
